pairs.question: Quando?
pairs.derivation: Imagined dialogue: Seneca says he has long experienced death (mors); Lucilius asks 'Quando?' inquis (framing 'inquis' dropped). Seneca answers 'Antequam nascerer.' Answer ends at first full stop, before the elaboration 'Mors est non esse.'

pairs.question: Quid in causa putas esse?
pairs.derivation: Seneca poses the question about the sleepless man of section 7 and answers it himself in the next sentence. Answer cut at first full stop, before the prescriptive elaboration 'Hic placandus est...'

pairs.question: Nunc me putas de Stoicis dicere, qui existimant animam hominis magno pondere extriti permanere non posse et statim spargi, quia non fuerit illi exitus liber?
pairs.derivation: Seneca asks whether Lucilius thinks he is speaking with the Stoics and answers in his own voice 'Ego vero non facio' (period). The following 'qui hoc dicunt videntur mihi errare' elaborates and is cut.

pairs.question: Ergo commune aliquod quaerendum est his omnibus vinculum, quod illa complectatur et sub se habeat. Hoc quid est?
pairs.derivation: Setup sentence kept verbatim so 'Hoc' has a referent (the common bond of homo/equus/canis). The one-word answer 'animal' (normalized capitalization) directly answers 'Hoc quid est?'; cut before 'Ergo genus esse coepit...'

pairs.question: Quid ista mihi subtilitas proderit?
pairs.derivation: Lucilius asks (framing 'inquis' dropped from within the quoted speech); Seneca answers directly 'Si me interrogas, nihil.' Answer is the full answering sentence to the first full stop, before the 'sed quemadmodum...' contrast.

pairs.question: Quid ergo, stulti ac mali non gaudent?
pairs.answer: Non magis quam praedam nancti leones.
pairs.derivation: Lucilius's question with framing 'inquis' dropped; 'Quid ergo' is the speaker's own words, kept. Seneca answers 'Non magis quam praedam nancti leones.' (first full stop), before the 'cum fatigaverunt se vino...' expansion.
